# Temple Scroll Column 15 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 15 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 15:3 — "perpetual burnt offering" vs. "regular daily burnt offering" (recurring)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the perpetual burnt offering" | Literal olat ha-tamid |
| LOGOS | "the perpetual burnt offering" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the regular daily burnt offering" | Clarifies the practical meaning of tamid |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "perpetual burnt offering" (EMET/LOGOS), consistent with Column 14 ruling.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Consistent with established precedent.

---

## 15:12 — "sons of Israel" vs. "children of Israel" vs. "Israelites"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the sons of Israel" | Literal bene Yisra'el |
| LOGOS | "the children of Israel" | Standard formal rendering; gender-inclusive |
| PNEUMA | "the Israelites" | Most natural modern English equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "children of Israel" (LOGOS). This is the traditional rendering that balances accuracy with readability. "Sons" (EMET) is unnecessarily gendered for a term that includes the entire community. "Israelites" (PNEUMA) is acceptable but loses the familial/covenantal resonance of bene.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 15:13-14 — vacat notation — how to represent blank lines

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "vacat" | Standard manuscript notation for intentional blank space |
| LOGOS | "[vacat]" | Bracketed to signal editorial notation |
| PNEUMA | "[blank line in manuscript]" | Explanatory note for general readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "[vacat]" (LOGOS). The bracketed vacat is the standard convention in Dead Sea Scrolls scholarship for marking intentional blank spaces. PNEUMA's expansion, while helpful, is unnecessarily verbose. EMET's unbracketed vacat could be confused with translated text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
